notes:
- Profiles open in one request now: your bio, banner and favourites used to wait for the whole media list to download - one request per 500 entries - before anything was drawn, even though only two of the five tabs read it. The page appears as soon as AniList answers, and the two tabs that need the list say they are still counting instead of showing zeroes as if they were your totals.
- Two more statuses to filter by: On Hiatus and Cancelled. The cards have drawn those chips all along, but the filter had no way to ask for them, so a cancelled entry could be seen and not searched for.
- Bios render more of what AniList actually accepts: `~~~a centred line~~~`, a parenthesised video or clip URL, and a title underlined with `===`. Fixed with them: a URL ending a sentence no longer swallows the full stop, and an email address in a bio is no longer turned into a username mention.
- Tier lists are saved projects now: the trophy opens a list of your lists instead of dropping you straight onto a board, so one ranking no longer has to be everything you have. Carry on with the one you used last, open any of them, make a new empty one, or rename and delete the ones you are done with - and every list is saved as its own document, so editing one no longer rewrites the others.
- Drag and drop you can aim: dropping a poster between two others now puts it exactly there, a caret shows the seam it will land on, and the hint naming that tier stays pinned on screen while you drag. Holding a tile near the top or bottom edge scrolls the screen for you, so a row that is off-screen is reachable without letting go - and the tile stays under your finger while it scrolls.
- Undo: every edit to a list offers to be taken back, named for what it would undo, including removing a tier and the titles filed under it. "Empty every tier" keeps your tiers and colours and puts the titles back.
- A bug that could rename a row out from under you: renaming a tier to something containing a comma broke the stored format, and the row came back mangled. Names are escaped now, so a tier can be called whatever you like.
